strings.d1.s0.name: Icherisheher Eski Şehir
strings.d1.s0.tips: A walled 12th-century city and UNESCO site: narrow lanes, the location where the film Brilliant Hand (Elmas Kol) was shot, and carpet sellers.
strings.d1.s1.name: Maiden Tower
strings.d1.s1.tips: A mysterious 8-storey tower (Zoroastrian, perhaps?). From the top you can see the Caspian Sea and the Flame Towers.
strings.d1.s2.name: Palace of the Shirvanshahs
strings.d1.s2.tips: The 15th-century palace of the Shirvanshahs, with a mausoleum, a divan house and a hammam.
strings.d1.s3.name: Firuze Restoranı Eski Şehir
strings.d1.s3.tips: Azerbaijani cuisine: kutab (thin stuffed flatbread), piti (lamb and chickpea stew) and saj (meat and vegetables cooked on a griddle).
strings.d1.s4.name: Baku Boulevard
strings.d1.s4.tips: A 3.7 km promenade (1909) along the Caspian shore, with a Ferris wheel and gondolas in Little Venice. After 20:00 take the funicular up to Highland Park and watch the Flame Towers light show.
strings.d1.b0.name: Sehirli Tendir
strings.d1.b0.tips: Tandir bread (baked in a clay oven) and kutab, on an Old City street.
strings.d1.b1.name: Museum of Miniature Books
strings.d1.b1.tips: Guinness record-holding miniature books. Free entry; an alternative to the palace.
strings.d2.theme: Heydar Aliyev and the Carpet Museum
strings.d2.s0.name: Heydar Aliyev Center
strings.d2.s0.tips: Zaha Hadid's wavy white masterpiece, with a classic car exhibition. Photographing the exterior is free.
strings.d2.s1.name: Azerbaijan Carpet Museum
strings.d2.s1.tips: A building shaped like a rolled carpet, on the Boulevard, with weaving demonstrations.
strings.d2.s2.name: Nargiz Restaurant Bulvar
strings.d2.s2.tips: Azerbaijani food with Caspian views: dolma and kebab.
strings.d2.s3.name: Nizami Street Torgovaya
strings.d2.s3.tips: A pedestrian shopping street lined with 19th-century oil baron buildings.
strings.d2.s4.name: Baku Crystal Hall & Flag Square Walk
strings.d2.s4.tips: The Eurovision 2012 arena. Watch the sunset at the end of the Boulevard.
strings.d2.b0.name: Museum of Modern Art Baku
strings.d2.b0.tips: Azerbaijani modern art; an alternative to the carpet museum.
strings.d2.b1.name: Paul's Bakery Fountains Square
strings.d2.b1.tips: Coffee and pastries on the square.
strings.d3.s0.name: Gobustan Rock Art
strings.d3.s0.tips: 60 km south (tour about 40 AZN, or take a taxi). More than 6,000 rock carvings up to 10,000 years old, a UNESCO site, with a museum.
strings.d3.s1.name: Gobustan Mud Volcanoes
strings.d3.s1.tips: Azerbaijan has half of the world's mud volcanoes: bubbling cones of cold mud, reached by old Lada.
strings.d3.s2.name: Bibi-Heybat Mosque
strings.d3.s2.tips: A mosque on the Caspian shore, destroyed by the Soviets and later rebuilt, set among oil pumpjacks.
strings.d3.s3.name: Qobustan Yolu Balık Lokantası
strings.d3.s3.tips: Caspian fish (kutum) and levengi (stuffed fish or chicken), on the way.
strings.d3.s4.name: Yanar Dag
strings.d3.s4.tips: A gas-fed hillside that has burned continuously for 60 years, tied to Zoroastrian tradition. Striking in the dark of evening, 25 km north.
strings.d3.b0.name: Ateshgah Fire Temple
strings.d3.b0.tips: The Surakhani Zoroastrian-Hindu fire temple, in the same direction as Yanar Dag. Visit instead of it or as an addition.
strings.d3.b1.name: Qala Köy Restoranı
strings.d3.b1.tips: Tandir and saj next to the ethnographic village; an alternative to the roadside restaurant.
strings.d4.s0.name: Ateshgah of Baku
strings.d4.s0.tips: The Surakhani fire temple (17th-century Hindu-Zoroastrian), with a natural gas flame and pilgrim cells.
strings.d4.s1.name: Qala Archaeological Ethnographic Complex
strings.d4.s1.tips: An open-air museum village on the Absheron peninsula, with a fortress, tandir ovens and camels.
strings.d4.s2.name: Mardakan Fortress & Town
strings.d4.s2.tips: A 14th-century fortress and arboretum, plus Yesenin's house.
strings.d4.s3.name: Mardakan Balık Tavernası
strings.d4.s3.tips: Grilled fish in a seaside town.
strings.d4.s4.name: Bilgah Beach
strings.d4.s4.tips: The winter Caspian wind and a walk along the shore.
strings.d4.b0.name: Amburan Beach Club
strings.d4.b0.tips: A beach club with sun loungers, in Bilgah.
strings.d4.b1.name: Gala Köyü Çayhanesi
strings.d4.b1.tips: Tea in pear-shaped glasses with jam, in the village.
strings.d5.s0.name: Sheki Khan's Palace
strings.d5.s0.tips: 4 hours from Baku (early tour or car; staying overnight is ideal). A palace built in 1762 with shebeke stained glass, a UNESCO site, built without nails.
strings.d5.s1.name: Sheki Caravanserai
strings.d5.s1.tips: An 18th-century caravanserai hotel, with a courtyard and vaults.
strings.d5.s2.name: Şeki Piti Öğle Gagarin
strings.d5.s2.tips: Sheki's piti soup served in an earthenware pot (the ritual: first dip bread in the broth, then mash the meat). Try Sheki halva too.
strings.d5.s3.name: Kish Albanian Church
strings.d5.s3.tips: A Caucasian Albanian church (legend dates it to the 1st century), linked to Thor Heyerdahl's theory, in the village.
strings.d5.s4.name: Şeki Halva Atölyesi
strings.d5.s4.tips: Sheki halva to take home, on the way back (Baku 20:00).
strings.d5.b0.name: Gabala Tufandag Cable Car
strings.d5.b0.tips: A Caucasus mountain cable car and Lake Nohur; closer than Sheki (3 hours), so a good alternative.
strings.d5.b1.name: Lahıc Köy Çayhanesi
strings.d5.b1.tips: Tea and kebab in a cobbled coppersmith village; an alternative on the road to Sheki.
strings.d6.s0.name: Taza Bazaar
strings.d6.s0.tips: A local market: pomegranates, saffron, sumac, cheese tasting and dried fruit.
strings.d6.s1.name: Baku Funicular & Martyrs' Lane Daytime
strings.d6.s1.tips: See Martyrs' Lane and the Eternal Flame by day, plus the Turkish Martyrs' Mosque.
strings.d6.s2.name: Sumakh Restaurant
strings.d6.s2.tips: Stylish Azerbaijani cuisine: saj and kutab, in Khagani.
strings.d6.s3.name: Baku Sea Boat Tour
strings.d6.s3.tips: A 1-hour Caspian boat tour from the Boulevard, with the skyline views.
strings.d6.s4.name: Nizami Cinema & Passage Cafes Evening
strings.d6.s4.tips: Seaside Park and the tea houses of Torgovaya, with shisha.
strings.d6.b0.name: Stone Chronicle Museum
strings.d6.b0.tips: A museum of stone inscriptions, on the Boulevard.
strings.d6.b1.name: Çay Bağı 145 Eski Şehir
strings.d6.b1.tips: Tea and jam in the Old City, in the Azerbaijani tea tradition.
strings.d7.theme: Boulevard morning and a gentle farewell
strings.d7.s0.name: Little Venice Boulevard Morning Walk
strings.d7.s0.tips: Canals with gondolas and morning calm.
strings.d7.s1.name: Mugham Center
strings.d7.s1.tips: A building shaped like a tar (a stringed instrument), on the Boulevard. See it from outside.
strings.d7.s2.name: Qaynana Restoranı Kahvaltı
strings.d7.s2.tips: Azerbaijani breakfast: clotted cream, honey, tandir bread and kuymak (a cornmeal and cheese dish), next to Fountains Square.
strings.d7.s3.name: Baku Airport Bus H1
strings.d7.s3.tips: The H1 bus runs from 28 May and takes 40 minutes (BakıKart). Time to say goodbye.
strings.d7.b0.name: Ali and Nino Kitapçı Kafe
strings.d7.b0.tips: Breakfast in a bookshop cafe, in the city of the novel.
strings.d7.b1.name: Government House
strings.d7.b1.tips: A giant Stalin-era building on Azadliq Square. See it from outside.
strings.note0: BakıKart (metro/bus 0.50 AZN); Bolt taxis are cheap. Take the H1 bus to the airport. For Gobustan and Sheki, join a tour or hire a car.
strings.note1: Winter is windy at 2-8°C; March brings Novruz (spring festival, fire jumping). April-May and September-October are ideal, and Sheki in autumn is golden.
strings.note2: Turkish citizens get 30 days visa-free (with ID card from 2025). 1 manat ≈ 0.6 USD; kutab 2 AZN, piti 8, restaurant meals 20-30, museums 5-15; tip 10%.
strings.note3: The Flame Towers light up after 21:00; Yanar Dag is best in the evening; Heydar Aliyev Center is closed on Mondays.
strings.note4: Piti, kutab, plov (shah plov), dolma, levengi, Sheki halva, pomegranate juice, tea in pear-shaped glasses with jam.
strings.note5: Turkish is understood (Azerbaijani Turkish); Russian is widely spoken. An oil city: look for the pumpjacks at Bibi-Heybat.
